site.name: Bachelor–Syracuse Mine Tour
site.location: Gold Hill north of Ouray, Ouray County
overview: The Bachelor–Syracuse is a historic precious-metal mine on Gold Hill north of Ouray. The modern visitor entrance uses the lower Syracuse Level, one part of a larger Bachelor mining system that also included older upper workings and the nearby mining settlement known as Ash.

timeline.text: Historical references place the beginning of the Bachelor Mine in the 1880s. Charlie Armstrong, George Hurlburt, and J. Frank Sanders were early owners, and rich ore supported intensive development even through the silver-price collapse of 1893.
Investors from Syracuse, New York financed the lower Syracuse Level. The tunnel became an important producing and access working and later became the underground route used for public mine tours.
Federal Defense Minerals Administration records list the Bachelor Mine in Ouray County as a lead-zinc, silver, gold, and copper property under Bachelor Development Company.
The property has continued as a tourist mine. Colorado mining regulators have documented the Bachelor Mine as an underground operation that also supports public mine tours.

moreHistory: The Bachelor property was more than one opening. Ore from the upper mine moved down Red Canyon toward Bachelor Switch, while the settlement of Ash developed near the mine with a mill, school, post office, and band. The lower Syracuse Level is a distinct component of that larger system and is the most appropriate visitor-facing identification point for the modern Bachelor–Syracuse Mine Tour. Published sources disagree on the exact discovery year, so this record does not assign a more precise origin date than the 1880s.
